title: Why Your AI Agents Can't Talk to Each Other (Yet) — Vlad Luzin, BAND
talk_summary: A vendor pitch from BAND arguing that multi-agent systems are already common but that messaging platforms and low-level protocols (MCP/A2A) are poor transports for agent-to-agent communication. The genuinely transferable content is the diagnosis of why ad-hoc multi-agent wiring fails: statelessness, one-way calls, missing discovery, and no shared run/session identity mapping.

takeaways.technique: Persistent stateful agent sessions instead of stateless tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Argue that MCP-style stateless calls break multi-agent work because you cannot return to the same agent and ask what happened; they keep agents as stateful, addressable participants in a shared conversation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: MCP means stateless calls. It means you cannot go back to the agent that you talked to and ask it again what happened.

takeaways.technique: Runtime binding: map thread/session/execution/run IDs across agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Identify 'runtime binding' as the hard unsolved piece: connecting a thread ID to a session ID to an execution ID to a run ID so multiple agents work toward the same goal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to connect a thread ID to a session ID to execution ID to a run ID of this multiple agents

takeaways.technique: Agent registry with bilateral-consent contact requests
takeaways.evidence_quote: We are sending a contact request that requires a bilateral consent from both parties

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents can invite a human into the same conversational space when they struggle, giving full visibility into agent-to-agent exchanges.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if they struggle and Mike struggles, uh these agents can invite me into the same conversation space

takeaways.technique: Observability spanning messages and subsequent tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Argue observability must cover not just message delivery between agents but which tool calls happened after an agent received a message, across distributed systems.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Observability not in a message that was sent from agent A on server A to agent B on server B. But also what tool calls

takeaways.technique: Avoid building custom transport; use a shared conversation layer
takeaways.what_they_do: Claim that wiring agents via REST/MCP/A2A forces you to reimplement queues, retries, persistence, and discovery, and pitch a hosted conversation layer instead.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're basically building planning. You're not building a multi-agent system. You're wasting your time on a boring boring stuff.
